solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I should return bearing reserve

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the short form for 'I should' is read backwards

parts.note: I'D is the contraction of 'I should' or 'I would'
one's bearing or posture is one's stance

explanation.surface: Someone resolving to go back and keep their dignified bearing in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I should' shortens to the contraction I'D, a standard crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve in the sense of aloofness or coolness of manner is keeping people at a distance.

clue.text: Elegant doctor, he's so shy in every other case

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the words 'he's so shy' leaves only alternate characters

explanation.surface: A smart-dressed medic who is nonetheless bashful in company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in every other case' takes the alternate letters E, S, S, Y from HE'S SO SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe clothing or appearance that is smart and stylish, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Beetle succeeded with motor rating, eg

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
a motor is a car
an able seaman, AB, is an example of a naval rating

explanation.surface: A Volkswagen Beetle triumphing in a motoring assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: A naval rating is a sailor below officer rank; AB (able-bodied seaman) is the classic crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, held sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Wrong smoker's accessory husband's flung out

indicators.note: flinging something out removes it, so the husband's letter is dropped from the accessory

parts.note: an ashtray is a dish for a smoker's ash
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife hurls her husband's ashtray out of the house, perhaps wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Going astray means going off course, which is going wrong.

clue.text: Harmony in a contract

parts.note: acting in concert means acting in harmony
taken as written

explanation.surface: Seems to praise the goodwill written into a legal agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun for a legal agreement, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To concertina is to fold up or collapse like the bellows of that instrument, that is, to shrink.

clue.text: Relaxed dropping stone into marsh grass

indicators.note: dropping something into another puts it inside, so the stone abbreviation goes in
into says the stone letters go inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of marshes
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: Someone unwinding by tossing a pebble into the reeds.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is a stone, the British unit of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Having rested, one is relaxed; both are past forms meaning took it easy.

clue.text: Make enemy of sergeant recklessly

indicators.note: acting recklessly means acting wildly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A soldier rashly falls out with his sergeant.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone, turning a friend into an adversary, is the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Fantastic artificer lacking lead: dreadful

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly imagined, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the lead of a word is its first letter, which goes missing here

explanation.surface: A craftsman without his leading role is a dreadful flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' looks like the definition, a common sense of the answer, but it is the anagram signal; 'lacking lead' drops the opening A of ARTIFICER to leave RTIFICER.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense the word means terrifying or frightful, from the same root as terror.

clue.text: Horror story is seen in dead flower

indicators.note: something seen in another is found inside it, so the small word sits within

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A grim tale in which a wilted bloom appears.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale of catastrophe, where everything goes terribly wrong, is a calamity in everyday terms.

clue.text: Demanding much — no longer acting

parts.note: EX means former, no longer so
taken as written

explanation.surface: A retired actor with exacting standards for fees.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that is strict and asks a lot of effort is described as rigorous in that way.

clue.text: Opening from Saracens' hooker (small) sets the ball rolling

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a hooker is slang for a prostitute, as is tart

explanation.surface: A small rugby hooker for the Saracens club kicks off the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Saracens is an English rugby union club, and a hooker is a front-row forward; here it means a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: To set the ball rolling is to begin something, an idiom for commencing.

clue.text: Captain, say, is wise man hanging on to a remote

indicators.note: hanging on to something means holding it, so the wise man's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: a seer is a prophet or sage
remote means far away

explanation.surface: A sage clutches a television remote control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remote' looks like a TV gadget, but it is the adjective meaning distant.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's captain is an example of a sailor, so 'say' signals an example definition.

clue.text: Sends message from close to Gibraltar — cheerio

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: adios is Spanish for goodbye, as cheerio is British slang

explanation.surface: A goodbye message beamed from near the Rock of Gibraltar.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheerio is a casual British goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit a message over the airwaves by wireless is the verb meaning here.

clue.text: In large lathe being refashioned

indicators.note: refashioning something gives it a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big machine tool being rebuilt in a workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In' as an adjective means fashionable, the current craze, which the phrase also means.

clue.text: POW camp force, we hear, is rising in cave

parts.note: a Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for force is said aloud and spelt by its sound

parts.note: might means strength or force

explanation.surface: Rumours of military force at a prison camp rising up.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral column building upward from a cavern floor is exactly this formation, as opposed to one hanging down.

clue.text: Food wrapper? Mine's down there!

parts.note: egg is slang for a mine or bomb, so 'mine's' gives the possessive of that word
hell is traditionally the place down below

explanation.surface: Someone asks about packaging and declares their own is in the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Mine's down there' as EGG'S HELL, the place below for a mine; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The brittle casing around a hen's egg is nature's own packaging for food.

clue.text: Child given small railway and soldiers

parts.note: an infant is a young child
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A child given a toy train set and toy soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers collectively make up this branch of an army.

clue.text: A lemon is lost in pud

indicators.note: letters that are lost have strayed from their places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook finds the lemon has disappeared into the pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk pudding made from wheat grains is a classic British school dessert.

clue.text: Biccies spice up being out to lunch

parts.note: to ginger something up is to liven or spice it up
out to lunch is slang for crazy, as is nuts

explanation.surface: Someone frantically jazzing up their biscuits while away at lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Biccies is British slang for biscuits (cookies).
explanation.definitionFit: These are hard spiced ginger cookies, a classic British biscuit for dunking in tea.

clue.text: Party cheats conservative sorts blind to change

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
to do someone is to cheat or swindle them

explanation.surface: Swindlers at a party who are old-fashioned and resist all reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a dodo means they are hopelessly old-fashioned, after the extinct bird.

clue.text: Evil intent from maiden, someone who had adventures?

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
Alice had adventures in Wonderland in Lewis Carroll's book

explanation.surface: A young woman's adventures hide a wicked motive.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over in which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is spite, the wish to do harm, which is wicked purpose.

clue.text: Fantastic cress sandwiches, English niche

indicators.note: to sandwich is to enclose, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece
fantastic suggests something wildly imagined, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Marvellous English cress sandwiches, a niche taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' rearranges CRESS to RCESS, which 'sandwiches' round E.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove set back into a wall is both a niche and this word.

clue.text: Main offspring is mature salt

definitions.meaning: to mature, as timber or wine does over time
to add salt or flavouring to food

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a son is male offspring

explanation.surface: A sailor's son grows up salty.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber is matured by drying, and food is flavoured with salt; the verb covers both.

clue.text: Last month speak in court to confer award

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the last month of the year
to orate is to speak formally, as a barrister does before a court

explanation.surface: Last month someone addressed a royal court to present an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour someone with a medal is the sense of decorating them.

clue.text: Scoff at wickedness? Gets pizza, stays home, —- —

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily
sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at sin while ordering a pizza and staying in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff at' looks like 'mock', but scoff is British slang for eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a takeaway meal at home rather than going out is dining at home.

clue.text: Saint Charlie before long is earl

parts.note: Charlie is the NATO alphabet word for C
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A holy Charlie who will soon be an earl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning make a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare someone officially a saint in the church is the verb meaning here.

clue.text: Produce chap, parishioner who lacks expert knowhow

parts.note: hens produce eggs, that is, they lay them
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A churchgoer making things without proper expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-cleric church member, or a non-specialist in any field, is described by this word.

clue.text: Have second thoughts about bums on seats finally

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
bums is slang for backsides, as is asses

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word seats

explanation.surface: A theatre producer reconsidering how many paying customers are sitting down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bums on seats' is a British idiom for audience numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate something again after more thought is to rethink or reconsider it.
